type: authored manuscript-fragment fixtures; not real held-out papers

cases.prompt: The paper introduces a new attention layer. Experiments report accuracy on MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval in a result table. No task construction or evaluation setup is described. Create appropriate paper figures.

Section 3 introduces a benchmark built by collecting public tables, annotating questions and answer spans, rejecting ambiguous items, and splitting by source document. Section 4 supplies questions and tables to models; answers are scored against withheld references. Design the appropriate figures.

Section 4.1 uses an existing warehouse simulator. Each episode starts at a sampled shelf, exposes a local camera and inventory, permits move/pick/place actions, ends at delivery or 100 steps, and scores delivery plus collision penalties. The paper proposes only the policy. Show its experimental setup.
The related-work section surveys WebArena, OSWorld, and embodied agent benchmarks. This paper itself proves a generalization bound and contains no evaluated benchmark or environment.

Only a title and abstract are supplied: We introduce ExampleBench, a comprehensive evaluation suite. The abstract lists an aggregate model ranking but gives no task definition, source instances, or scoring workflow. Decide whether enough setup evidence is present to draw it.

Please produce all three standard figure types. Available manuscript: low-rank operator derivation, optimizer architecture, and a table of final CIFAR accuracy. No benchmark setup or protocol is provided.

Appendix B describes an adaptation of a navigation benchmark: original scenes and action space are retained, observations receive controlled occlusions, each condition uses the same start-goal pairs, and success is arrival within 1 meter before timeout. Draw the setup and identify the adaptation.

Our method embeds a token into a latent environment vector and applies a recurrent attention operator. Environment here names a learned feature. The supplied paper contains algebra and a method definition only.

Section 2 defines seeded task generators with configurable difficulty. Each instance contains a question, private solution metadata, and a task-specific score function. A model produces one response. No persistent state or action loop exists.
Draw the environment figure for our benchmark. We have not supplied the paper, protocol, task, observation, action, or scoring definition.

Section 3 describes benchmark construction from repository commits: mine bug-fix pairs, reconstruct the pre-fix container, retain instances whose new tests fail before the fix and pass afterward, and package issue text with the starting repository. Evaluation applies a submitted patch and runs the held-out tests.

The evaluation section explains an existing summarization setup: each model sees a news article, returns a summary under the same length cap, and blinded human raters score factual consistency and coverage using a specified rubric. The contribution is a new model.
The method diagram contains a frozen teacher, training labels, distillation loss, and student updates. No evaluation task or benchmark setup is described in the supplied manuscript.

Section 3 introduces a video interaction benchmark. Perception tasks expose full clips. Interaction tasks expose only a prefix, ask whether to interrupt, then score generated replies using withheld future-context annotations. Different access conditions must remain distinct.
